_comment: Every table or field a reconciliation fixture carries with no diya-gl master data behind it, and every literal extract-scenarios.js states in its own source instead of deriving from a master. Produced by T1 (PLAN_ROUNDTRIP_FIDELITY.md), consumed by T1b, which extends each master and moves the extractor's own literals onto it.

backedSections.note: 1 row, £12,000 Ford Transit van, matches the master's one 5900-coded purchase line

gaps.reason: master has no stock account (1100) or opening/closing stock figure
master has no debtor ledger and no trade debtors account (1300)
same as opening_debtors
master declares trade creditors (2100) in its chart of accounts but carries no opening/closing creditor ledger
same as opening_creditors

backedSections.note: 1 row, £200 dashcam and vehicle signage, matches the master's 7000-coded purchase line (Amazon, 'Nextbase dashcam')
matches master employees[] (Mike Brown, Tom Davies)
master has 24 payroll lines (2 employees x 12 months); field values not cross-checked figure by figure

gaps.reason: master has no bank journal at all: no opening balance, customer receipts, supplier payments, net pay, PAYE or CIS remittance lines
master has no stock account or opening/closing stock figure
master has no debtor ledger
same as opening_debtors
master has no creditor ledger
same as opening_creditors

no VAT-registered BrickWork master exists; every section (sales, purchases, bank, payroll, employees, debtors, creditors, stock, business) is hand-stated. The plan's decision is to derive this fixture from the non-VAT brickwork-pro master by a declared 1.5x-scale-plus-VAT build section, not a second master directory.
master has no bank journal
master has no opening balance journal (no documentReference starting OB-), so buildOpeningBalance() finds nothing to reverse-engineer
master has no stock account or figure
master has no debtor ledger
same as opening_debtors
master has no creditor ledger
same as opening_creditors
master declares Mike Brown's 100 shares only on directors[], not on a separate members[] table; derivable the same way precision-code-ltd's fullMembers is, but the table itself does not exist yet
master entityInformation has no address fields
same as se-brickwork-pro-vat: no VAT-registered BrickWork master exists, derive by the declared scale-and-VAT build section instead of a second master

backedSections.note: 52 weekly settlements, matches the master's 52 sales lines

gaps.reason: the fixture has no [[fixed_asset_additions]] table at all, but the master books a real £900 in-car camera system (7000-coded, 2025-05-12, 'Nextbase Fleet'). Adding it gives the fixture a capital allowance it has never claimed, moving the reconciled net profit figure -- this is a fixture gain T1b has to reconcile and re-baseline, not a silent addition.

backedSections.note: 180 daily fares, matches the master's 180 sales lines

gaps.reason: the fixture has no [[fixed_asset_additions]] table; the master's £200 dashcam is already captured by the bst-sp-sixty fixture instead. Whether Taxi's own Fixed Assets schedule (vehicles only, per the excel skill) should also claim it is a T1b product-scope decision, not a data gap.

no master exists (no examples/basic-taxi-driver/ or equivalent) and the fixture has no [business] table at all -- 180 daily fares totalling 36,000, 21 purchase rows, one £8,000 vehicle (5900-coded 'fixed_asset_additions'), and no entity name, address, UTR or NINO anywhere. The plan creates examples/basic-taxi-driver/ from scratch for this one.

extractorLiterals.name: openingDebtors
extractorLiterals.reason: stated directly (Acme Corp, Beta Systems, Gamma Ltd invoices); not derived from any master line or book table, even though precision-code-ltd is the extractor-driven master

extractorLiterals.name: bstClosingDebtors
extractorLiterals.reason: stated directly; the BST subset carries no bank journal to settle an invoice against, so nothing is derivable without one

extractorLiterals.name: openingCreditors
extractorLiterals.reason: stated directly; no opening creditor journal or ledger exists in the master to derive it from

extractorLiterals.name: closingCreditors
extractorLiterals.reason: stated directly, for the same reason as openingCreditors; unlike closingDebtors there is no bank-settlement derivation for creditors

extractorLiterals.name: straddlingSales / straddlingPurchases
extractorLiterals.reason: VAT-straddling entries the VAT workbook's own out-of-year sheets take, entered directly on the scenario TOML. No diya-gl line carries a diya-gl:vatPeriodEnd today (the v2 field this track adds), so there is no master representation to derive them from at either the line or book level

extractorLiterals.name: hpAgreements
extractorLiterals.reason: the agreement terms (finance company, admin charges, total interest, term) are a literal; only the two purchases the agreements finance exist as real master lines (carrying diya-gl:hpAgreement). The v2 book.toml's own hpAgreements[] table (added directly to the master by this track) is not yet read by the extractor, which still emits the subset's copy from this same literal

extractorLiterals.name: openingFixedAssets (tax_wdv field only)
extractorLiterals.reason: cost and accumulated depreciation match the master's own opening balance journal (accounts 0030/0040) exactly, but the written-down tax value each asset carries forward (24000 for the van) has no source anywhere in the master; it is a bare literal the capital allowances working needs and nothing in book.toml states

extractorLiterals.name: chargesRegister
extractorLiterals.reason: the one registered charge (NatWest fixed charge over the delivery van) is entirely a literal; no line or book field in the master names a charge, a chargeholder or its terms
